t.pt: ใกล้ 'perto' e ไกล 'longe' pedem complementos diferentes
t.en: ใกล้ 'near' and ไกล 'far' take different complements

e.pt: As duas palavras se distinguem só pelo tom: ใกล้ é 'perto', ไกล é 'longe'. E cada uma pede um complemento diferente. Para 'longe de' entra o จาก — ไกลจากกรุงเทพฯ ('longe de Bangkok'). Para 'perto de' entra o กับ — อยู่ใกล้กับกรุงเทพฯ ('fica perto de Bangkok'). Na fala rápida o กับ encurta para กะ, e aí vem o detalhe que o livro destaca: o กะ só pode aparecer quando a palavra seguinte começa por consoante; antes de vogal ele se colaria nela, então volte ao กับ.
e.en: ใกล้ 'near' and ไกล 'far' are told apart only by tone and take different complements: ไกล + จาก (ไกลจากกรุงเทพฯ 'far from Bangkok'), ใกล้ + กับ (อยู่ใกล้กับกรุงเทพฯ 'near Bangkok'). The colloquial reduced form กะ is possible after ใกล้ only when the following word begins with a consonant.

notas.ex: อยู่|yùu ใกล้|glâi กับ|gàp กรุงเทพฯ|grung-têep

t.pt: Dois jeitos de dizer a mesma distância
t.en: Two equivalent ways of stating a distance

e.pt: O livro mostra o par com as embaixadas, e o sentido é idêntico nos dois. O primeiro jeito toma um lugar como sujeito e traz o outro depois da preposição: สถานทูตอเมริกันอยู่ใกล้กับสถานทูตอังกฤษ ('a Embaixada Americana fica perto da Embaixada Britânica'). O segundo junta os dois lugares com กับ e fecha a frase com กัน, a partícula de reciprocidade: สถานทูตอเมริกันกับสถานทูตอังกฤษอยู่ใกล้กัน ('a Embaixada Americana e a Britânica ficam perto uma da outra'). É o nosso 'um do outro'. O mesmo molde vale para o lado do ไกล: X อยู่ไกลจาก Y = X กับ Y อยู่ไกลกัน.
e.en: Two equivalent patterns: สถานทูตอเมริกันอยู่ใกล้กับสถานทูตอังกฤษ 'the American Embassy is near the British Embassy' versus สถานทูตอเมริกันกับสถานทูตอังกฤษอยู่ใกล้กัน 'the American and the British Embassy are close to each other', where กัน marks reciprocity. The same alternation holds with ไกล: X อยู่ไกลจาก Y = X กับ Y อยู่ไกลกัน.

t.pt: Quão longe: a medida vai no fim
t.en: How far: the measure goes at the end

e.pt: Para informar a distância, a medida entra no fim da frase, depois dos dois lugares: กรุงเทพฯ อยู่ไกลจากเชียงใหม่ 900 กิโล ('Bangkok fica a 900 quilômetros de Chiang Mai'). A pergunta é igual, só que a medida vira กี่: ...กี่กิโล ('quantos quilômetros?'). O molde é lugar + verbo + lugar + extensão, na mesma ordem do nosso 'fica a 900 km de tal lugar' — não há preposição equivalente a 'a', o número simplesmente se apoia no fim.
e.en: The extent of the distance is placed at the end: NP + verb phrase + NP + extent, as in กรุงเทพฯ อยู่ไกลจากเชียงใหม่ 900 กิโล 'Bangkok is 900 kilometers from Chiangmai'. The question replaces the measure with กี่ (กี่กิโล).

t.en: มี 'there is' builds a subjectless sentence

e.pt: A estrutura é: lugar (opcional) + มี + substantivo (+ complemento). แถวนี้มีร้านตัดผม significa 'nesta região há uma barbearia' — e o livro faz questão de avisar que a frase não tem sujeito nenhum. É o nosso 'tem/há' impessoal: ninguém pratica a ação, o que existe simplesmente existe. Por isso a pergunta se resolve acrescentando ไหม no fim, sem inventar um sujeito: แถวนี้มีร้านตัดผมไหมครับ. O lugar pode até ser omitido quando o contexto já diz onde.
e.en: มี means 'to be in existence' in constructions like (location) + มี + NP (+ complement), e.g. แถวนี้มีร้านตัดผม 'in this area there is a barber shop'. The book stresses that such a sentence has no subject; the question is formed simply by adding ไหม, and the location may be dropped when the context supplies it.

notas.ex: แถว|tɛ̌ɛo นี้|níi มี|mii ร้านตัดผม|ráan-dtàt-pǒm
